items.title: Wilbert Tillman Interview, 1961-08-15
items.q: Well, John said if we could make a name for the Tulane Band, why not let's go and pull off and make up a band of ours own. And that's why we organized at the Young Tuxedo, because we pulled out from the Tulane, you see, and John made up his own band.

ctx.x: Oh yes, I think I heard about it back in the 1940s.

Yeah, well, I played that with Buck. And they had the, at that time, they had the Tulane Brass Band. Well, Tulane, I used to work with them on sax, and John was playing with them on clarinet. That was drummed by Al Landry, Tulane Band. Well, John said if we could make a name for the Tulane Band, why not let's go and pull off and make up a band of ours own. And that's why we organized at the Young Tuxedo, because we pulled out from the Tulane, you see, and John made up his own band.
What year were you playing with the Tulane Band, Wilbur?

items.title: Wilbert Tillman Interview, 1966-01-20
items.q: See now them people didn't know nobody in the Young Tuxedo band but me and John.

ctx.x: Well how do these men in the grass band get jobs anyway, huh? Well they get them all kinds of ways.

They get them through being members of organizations. They get them through friends that know them better than they know others. See if they, it's like if you have a friend, regardless of what he is, if you got something that you can do in his way, you give it to him. Now regardless of who he hired, it don't make no difference. You're looking to him. Yeah. You're looking to the void. See, now all you want boys to do is bring you a band. You understand? And that's the way it is with them boys. See now I had a…
What about the churches, do they ever get any jobs through churches? Who is that? You, I mean with your band. Do the churches ever hire brass bands? Well no, they never hire them.
